## Overview

Enable vLLM's existing custom all-reduce on AMD RDNA4 (gfx1200/gfx1201) GPUs connected by PCIe peer-to-peer, such as Radeon AI PRO R9700 workstations. Today every RDNA4 tensor-parallel group uses RCCL. Three commits:

1. **`[Kernel][ROCm]` page-align uncached IPC buffers.** This is a general ROCm fix: without it, custom all-reduce fails to initialize on some HIP runtimes.
2. **`[Kernel][Distributed]` optional release/acquire start barrier.** It makes the zero-copy path correct over non-coherent PCIe. It is off by default, so there is no behaviour change for existing platforms.
3. **`[ROCm][Distributed]` enable custom all-reduce on RDNA4** for TP=2, 4 and 8, with measured per-world-size size limits.

Related: #57059 (same stale-read root cause, on MI100), #57182, RFC #55916, #55917, #57767 (see "Relation to other PRs").

## Claims

- Decode TPOT, `--disable-custom-all-reduce` vs this PR (median of 3 interleaved rounds, 512 input / 128 output tokens):

  | Model | TP | c=1 | c=2 | c=4 | c=8 |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | Llama-3.3-70B FP8 (block) | 8 | **-14.9%** | **-12.8%** | **-9.6%** | -0.4% (RCCL in both arms) |
  | Muse-Glimmer-30B (BF16) | 4 | **-8.1%** | **-8.7%** | **-7.4%** | **-3.9%** |
  | Qwen3-14B (BF16) | 2 | **-4.0%** | **-4.2%** | **-4.1%** | **-3.8%** |

- Accuracy unchanged: GSM8K 5-shot is within noise for all three models.
- Correctness: with the existing relaxed start barrier, every all-reduce over PCIe reads stale data (500/500 wrong per size). With the release barrier, 0 are wrong at TP=2/4/8.
- No behaviour change on CUDA, MI300 or RDNA3:
  - the new barrier is a template flag that defaults to off;
  - RDNA4 enablement is gated on the architecture;
  - the IPC buffer fix only rounds up an allocation size.
- `--disable-custom-all-reduce` still turns it off.

## Validation

**Hardware**
- **Host A:** 4x Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201), one CPU socket. Used for TP=2 and TP=4.
- **Host B:** 8x Radeon AI PRO R9700S (gfx1201), 2x EPYC 9554, GPUs 0-3 on one socket and 4-7 on the other. Used for TP=8, plus TP=2/4 groups that span both sockets.
- On both hosts every GPU pair is PCIe peer-to-peer, and amdsmi reports the links as not cache-coherent.

**Tests**

```bash
pytest -v tests/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py
# Host B (8 GPUs): 72 passed, 1 skipped (Requires SM100)
# Host A (4 GPUs): 69 passed, 4 skipped (Requires SM100; TP=8 cases: not enough GPUs)
```

New tests:
- `test_custom_allreduce_producer_in_graph` (GPU; TP=2/4/8) reproduces the stale-read bug.
  - **Setup:** a kernel writes each input right before its all-reduce inside the same graph, and the sources are refilled with fresh values before every replay. Outputs are compared bit-exactly with `torch.distributed`.
  - **Reused buffer:** each size also runs with one input buffer reused by every all-reduce in the graph.
  - **Variants:** the communicator vLLM builds for the platform, and `release_start=True` with the 1-stage and 2-stage kernels forced. On RDNA4 it also asserts that vLLM chose the release barrier and the size limit.
  - **Negative control:** with the release barrier disabled on RDNA4, the platform-default case fails `torch.equal`.
- CPU tests (mocked amdsmi): `test_rocm_pcie_p2p_detection`, `test_rocm_is_fully_connected_over_pcie_only_on_rdna4`, `test_custom_allreduce_dispatch_max_size`.

`pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: all hooks pass.

**Stale reads.** Producer in the graph, 500 all-reduces per size:

| Start barrier | TP=2 (8-384 KiB) | TP=4 (8-384 KiB) | TP=8 (16 KiB-2 MiB) |
|---|---|---|---|
| relaxed (current) | every call wrong | every call wrong | every call wrong (tested 16-128 KiB) |
| release (this PR) | 0 wrong | 0 wrong, also with 2-stage forced | 0 wrong (auto, 1-stage, 2-stage) |

The release barrier adds 0.1-1.6 us per call at TP=4, and up to 2.7 us at TP=2.

**Size limits.** One-shot reads every peer's whole input over PCIe, so it beats RCCL's ring only while the message is latency-bound. Per call, HIP graph replay, custom vs RCCL:

| TP | Last sizes where custom wins | First sizes where RCCL wins | Limit (exclusive) |

| 2 | 1 MiB 53.4 vs 69.7 us, ~8 MiB 362 vs 443 | none up to the buffer size | 8 MiB (default buffer) |
| 4 | 128 KiB 32.3 vs 39.3, 192 KiB 40.8 vs 43.2 | 224 KiB 46.2 vs 45.6, 256 KiB 51.5 vs 48.6 | 192 KiB |
| 8 | 96 KiB 44.6 vs 55.1, 112 KiB 50.5 vs 53.0 | 128 KiB 56.5 vs 53.9, 192 KiB 66.4 vs 58.5 | 128 KiB |

On host B, TP=2 and TP=4 groups that span both sockets still beat RCCL at their limits:

| Group | Size | Custom | RCCL |
|---|---|---|---|
| TP=2, GPUs 0,4 | 8 MiB | 207.9 us | 247.3 us |
| TP=4, GPUs 0,1,4,5 | 192 KiB | 33.2 us | 36.2 us |

TP=2/4, host A. The cap sweep used hidden 2048 (4 KiB per token); the rows up to 256 KiB come from a second sweep at hidden 4096:

## Details

**Motivation.** RDNA4 workstations have no XGMI; GPUs talk over PCIe peer-to-peer. `RocmPlatform.use_custom_allreduce()` is false outside MI300, and `CustomAllreduce` rejects more than two GPUs that are not 1-hop XGMI. So every decode all-reduce goes through RCCL's ring: two per layer, from a few KiB to a few hundred KiB, each needing 2*(N-1) dependent PCIe steps. The one-shot custom kernel needs a single barrier.

**Commit 1: page-align uncached IPC buffers (`csrc/custom_all_reduce.cu`).**
- On ROCm, `allocate_shared_buffer_and_handle` allocates every shared buffer with `hipDeviceMallocUncached` and exports it with `hipIpcGetMemHandle`.
- Some HIP runtimes reject that export with `hipErrorInvalidValue` when the size of an uncached allocation is not a multiple of 4 KiB. Cached allocations of the same size export fine.
- `CustomAllreduce` allocates `meta_size() + max_size`, and `meta_size()` is 4864 bytes, so custom all-reduce fails to initialize (`RuntimeError: CUDA error: invalid argument`).
- The fix rounds the size up to 4 KiB on ROCm. The allocation path is shared by all ROCm GPUs. This commit could also be split into its own PR if preferred.

**Commit 2: optional release/acquire start barrier (kernel; no behaviour change).**
- **Root cause:** the kernels open with `barrier_at_start`, which uses relaxed flags and by design orders nothing written before the kernel. Under graphs, peers read each rank's registered input in place, and that input was just written by the previous kernel (the o_proj/down_proj GEMM). Over coherent links this works. Over non-coherent PCIe, peers read stale data until the producer's L2 is written back: every result in the stress test was wrong, and model output was garbage.
- **The barrier:** `barrier_at_start_release` publishes the flag with a system-scope release store. `custom_collective_common.cuh` had it until #60721 pruned it as unused; this commit restores it. On gfx1201 it compiles to `global_wb scope:SCOPE_SYS` before the store and `global_inv scope:SCOPE_DEV` after the wait.
- **Plumbing:** a `start_release` template flag on `cross_device_reduce_1stage/2stage`, and `release_start` in `init_custom_ar` and `CustomAllreduce` (default `False`). Existing callers launch the same instantiations as before.

**Commit 3: RDNA4 enablement.**
- `RocmPlatform.use_custom_allreduce()`: also true on RDNA4.
- `RocmPlatform.is_fully_connected()`: on RDNA4, true when every pair has an amdsmi PCIe link and `amdsmi_is_P2P_accessible`. `CustomAllreduce` also runs the runtime P2P check (`_can_p2p`) on RDNA4, as on CUDA.
- `CustomAllreduce` on RDNA4 always uses `release_start=True`. It sends messages at or above `ROCM_RDNA4_PCIE_CUSTOM_ALL_REDUCE_MAX_SIZES[world_size]` (`{2: 8 MiB, 4: 192 KiB, 8: 128 KiB}`) to RCCL. World size 6 is not in the table and keeps RCCL.
- `QuickAllReduce` is now constructed on RDNA4, but disables itself (MI300 only).

**Design notes / trade-offs.**
- **Gated on the architecture, not on amdsmi's coherence flag,** because the barrier choice and the size limits are measured on RDNA4 only. Enabling the release barrier on all ROCm, as #57182 proposes, would be a one-line follow-up once its MI300 cost is measured. It composes with this PR.
- **A dispatch limit (`_dispatch_max_size`) rather than a lower `max_size`,** as CUDA's `CUSTOM_ALL_REDUCE_MAX_SIZES` does. `max_size` also sizes the IPC buffers and the batch-invariant chunks, which keep their defaults. Batch invariance keeps its semantics: custom all-reduce takes every size, in `max_size` chunks.
- **One limit per world size.** At TP=8 the 2-stage kernel (256 KiB to 1.5 MiB) is 5-11% faster than RCCL again. A single exclusive limit cannot include it without the 128-192 KiB 1-stage range, which is 5-13% slower. A possible follow-up is to lower the 1-stage → 2-stage switch for RDNA4 at 8 GPUs.
- **RDNA3 is not enabled;** it needs separate validation.
- **CI gap.** vLLM CI has no RDNA GPUs. `test_custom_all_reduce.py` runs in the (optional) A100, MI300 and MI355 Distributed jobs. There the new test exercises the `release_start=True` instantiations and checks that the platform default is unchanged. The RDNA4 path was validated on the hosts above.

**Relation to other PRs.**
- **#57182 / #57059:** same stale-read root cause, on MI100 XGMI. #57182 switches all of ROCm to the release barrier, and the end barrier to system-scope loads, unconditionally. It no longer builds on main because #60721 removed `barrier_at_start_release`, which this PR restores. This PR leaves other platforms unchanged and adds a reproducer test.
- **#55917 (FlyDSL) and #57767 (native HIP RDNA3/4):** new opt-in backends behind env vars. This PR adds no backend and no env var. It enables vLLM's existing custom all-reduce on RDNA4, by default, where it is measured to win.

**AI assistance.** AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the investigation, code, tests, benchmarks and this description. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and benchmarks listed above.

Tested on 2x Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201, PCIe only). No correctness problems found, and with MTP3 decode was about 6% faster than both `--disable-custom-all-reduce` and the #57767 RDNA HIP all-reduce.

**Setup**
- 2x R9700 32 GB, each PCIe 4.0 x16 on an ASRock Rack ROMED8-2T (EPYC 7313P). The GPUs are on different root ports (2 hops). `amd-smi topology`: link type PCIE, access ENABLED both ways, cache coherency NC. `can_device_access_peer` True both ways; a 64 MiB `cuda:0 -> cuda:1` copy runs at 25.4 GiB/s.
- Host kernel 7.0.0, `iommu=pt`. vLLM v0.32.0rc2 built from source, torch 2.13.0+rocm10.1.0. The build also carries a few unrelated patches plus #57767 (opt-in, off unless `VLLM_ROCM_USE_RDNA_ALL_REDUCE=1`). This PR applied with one hand-merged hunk in `RocmPlatform.use_custom_allreduce()` (a conflict with #57767), so both are selectable in one image.
- Model: Qwen3.8-27B FP8, TP=2, bf16 KV cache, max-model-len 262144, max-num-seqs 2, max-num-batched-tokens 1024, MTP with 3 speculative tokens, `HSA_ENABLE_IPC_MODE_LEGACY=0` (dma-buf IPC).

**Arms** (same image, fresh server start for every block, startup log checked each time)
| arm | how | startup log |
|---|---|---|
| this PR | default | `Custom allreduce on RDNA4 over PCIe peer-to-peer: release start barrier, messages smaller than 8388608 bytes.` and `Using ['CUSTOM', 'PYNCCL']` |
| #57767 | `VLLM_ROCM_USE_RDNA_ALL_REDUCE=1` | `Enabled graph-only RDNA HIP all-reduce: gfx1201 TP2`, `Using ['RDNA_HIP', 'PYNCCL']` |
| off | `--disable-custom-all-reduce` | `Using ['PYNCCL']` |

All 12 server starts showed the expected line for their arm.

**Decode, MTP3** (t/s, mean ± sd over 3 rounds, arm order rotated each round; llama-benchy pp2048 / tg128, single request; SE = difference / standard error)
| depth | this PR | #57767 | off | PR vs off | PR vs #57767 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 73.70 ± 2.88 | 69.67 ± 2.90 | 69.25 ± 2.61 | +6.4% (2.0 SE) | +5.8% (1.7 SE) |
| 32K | 69.31 ± 1.96 | 65.59 ± 1.13 | 65.65 ± 2.46 | +5.6% (2.0 SE) | +5.7% (2.9 SE) |
| 120K | 57.15 ± 3.64 | 51.69 ± 2.42 | 55.32 ± 2.54 | +3.3% (0.7 SE) | +10.6% (2.2 SE) |

MTP acceptance per block: this PR 68.2 / 69.7 / 69.3%, #57767 67.8 / 65.0 / 67.3%, off 68.3 / 66.8 / 65.7%.

Prefill was about the same (pp2048: 2961 / 2892 / 2886 t/s), as expected since 1024-token prefill chunks are 10 MiB and still go to RCCL.

With MTP3, #57767 was no faster than off. Probably because it only handles graph steps with 1 token per request, so the MTP verify steps (2 requests x 4 tokens x 5120 x bf16 = 80 KiB) go to RCCL, while this PR covers them.

**Decode, MTP off** (t/s, 1 run per arm)
| depth | this PR | #57767 | off |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 35.39 | 34.92 | 33.45 |
| 32K | 32.45 | 32.24 | 30.96 |

**Correctness** (temperature 0, thinking off, same prompts on every arm)
- 30 arithmetic and word questions with known answers: 29/30 on all three arms, same miss on each (702 / 39 answered as 17.99).
- Needle recall at ~100K tokens (needle at 40% depth): found on all arms.
- 5 longer generations (200 tokens each): output identical across all three arms.
- llama-benchy coherence check at concurrency 1 and 2: passed on all arms.

**Stability**
- 10-minute soak on this PR's arm: 109 requests, 0 errors.
- KV cache pool: this PR's arm used 0-8K fewer tokens than off (344-352K vs 352K with MTP3, 404.6K vs 411.9K without MTP). About the same as #57767.

**Tests from this PR** (`tests/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py -k 'producer_in_graph or rdna4 or pcie_p2p or dispatch_max_size'`)
- `test_custom_allreduce_dispatch_max_size` (2), `test_rocm_pcie_p2p_detection` (3), `test_rocm_is_fully_connected_over_pcie_only_on_rdna4` (2): passed.
- `test_custom_allreduce_producer_in_graph` TP=2 (platform_default, release_1stage, release_2stage): passed. TP=4/8 skipped (2 GPUs).
  These first failed at init because of a duplicate import in the #57767 patch I also carry (noted on #57767); they pass with that line removed.

## Details

**Motivation.** RDNA4 workstations have no XGMI; GPUs talk over PCIe peer-to-peer. `RocmPlatform.use_custom_allreduce()` is false outside MI300, and `CustomAllreduce` rejects more than two GPUs that are not 1-hop XGMI. So every decode all-reduce goes through RCCL's ring: two per layer, from a few KiB to a few hundred KiB, each needing 2*(N-1) dependent PCIe steps. The one-shot custom kernel needs a single barrier.

**Commit 1: page-align uncached IPC buffers (`csrc/custom_all_reduce.cu`).**
- On ROCm, `allocate_shared_buffer_and_handle` allocates every shared buffer with `hipDeviceMallocUncached` and exports it with `hipIpcGetMemHandle`.
- Some HIP runtimes reject that export with `hipErrorInvalidValue` when the size of an uncached allocation is not a multiple of 4 KiB. Cached allocations of the same size export fine.
- `CustomAllreduce` allocates `meta_size() + max_size`, and `meta_size()` is 4864 bytes, so custom all-reduce fails to initialize (`RuntimeError: CUDA error: invalid argument`).
- The fix rounds the size up to 4 KiB on ROCm. The allocation path is shared by all ROCm GPUs. This commit could also be split into its own PR if preferred.

**Commit 2: optional release/acquire start barrier (kernel; no behaviour change).**
- **Root cause:** the kernels open with `barrier_at_start`, which uses relaxed flags and by design orders nothing written before the kernel. Under graphs, peers read each rank's registered input in place, and that input was just written by the previous kernel (the o_proj/down_proj GEMM). Over coherent links this works. Over non-coherent PCIe, peers read stale data until the producer's L2 is written back: every result in the stress test was wrong, and model output was garbage.
- **The barrier:** `barrier_at_start_release` publishes the flag with a system-scope release store. `custom_collective_common.cuh` had it until #60721 pruned it as unused; this commit restores it. On gfx1201 it compiles to `global_wb scope:SCOPE_SYS` before the store and `global_inv scope:SCOPE_DEV` after the wait.
- **Plumbing:** a `start_release` template flag on `cross_device_reduce_1stage/2stage`, and `release_start` in `init_custom_ar` and `CustomAllreduce` (default `False`). Existing callers launch the same instantiations as before.

**Commit 3: RDNA4 enablement.**
- `RocmPlatform.use_custom_allreduce()`: also true on RDNA4.
- `RocmPlatform.is_fully_connected()`: on RDNA4, true when every pair has an amdsmi PCIe link and `amdsmi_is_P2P_accessible`. `CustomAllreduce` also runs the runtime P2P check (`_can_p2p`) on RDNA4, as on CUDA.
- `CustomAllreduce` on RDNA4 always uses `release_start=True`. It sends messages at or above `ROCM_RDNA4_PCIE_CUSTOM_ALL_REDUCE_MAX_SIZES[world_size]` (`{2: 8 MiB, 4: 192 KiB, 8: 128 KiB}`) to RCCL. World size 6 is not in the table and keeps RCCL.
- `QuickAllReduce` is now constructed on RDNA4, but disables itself (MI300 only).

**Design notes / trade-offs.**
- **Gated on the architecture, not on amdsmi's coherence flag,** because the barrier choice and the size limits are measured on RDNA4 only. Enabling the release barrier on all ROCm, as #57182 proposes, would be a one-line follow-up once its MI300 cost is measured. It composes with this PR.
- **A dispatch limit (`_dispatch_max_size`) rather than a lower `max_size`,** as CUDA's `CUSTOM_ALL_REDUCE_MAX_SIZES` does. `max_size` also sizes the IPC buffers and the batch-invariant chunks, which keep their defaults. Batch invariance keeps its semantics: custom all-reduce takes every size, in `max_size` chunks.
- **One limit per world size.** At TP=8 the 2-stage kernel (256 KiB to 1.5 MiB) is 5-11% faster than RCCL again. A single exclusive limit cannot include it without the 128-192 KiB 1-stage range, which is 5-13% slower. A possible follow-up is to lower the 1-stage → 2-stage switch for RDNA4 at 8 GPUs.
- **RDNA3 is not enabled;** it needs separate validation.
- **CI gap.** vLLM CI has no RDNA GPUs. `test_custom_all_reduce.py` runs in the (optional) A100, MI300 and MI355 Distributed jobs. There the new test exercises the `release_start=True` instantiations and checks that the platform default is unchanged. The RDNA4 path was validated on the hosts above.

**Relation to other PRs.**
- **#57182 / #57059:** same stale-read root cause, on MI100 XGMI. #57182 switches all of ROCm to the release barrier, and the end barrier to system-scope loads, unconditionally. It no longer builds on main because #60721 removed `barrier_at_start_release`, which this PR restores. This PR leaves other platforms unchanged and adds a reproducer test.
- **#55917 (FlyDSL) and #57767 (native HIP RDNA3/4):** new opt-in backends behind env vars. This PR adds no backend and no env var. It enables vLLM's existing custom all-reduce on RDNA4, by default, where it is measured to win.

issue_comments.body:
Tested on 2x Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201, PCIe only). No correctness problems found, and with MTP3 decode was about 6% faster than both `--disable-custom-all-reduce` and the #57767 RDNA HIP all-reduce.

**Setup**
- 2x R9700 32 GB, each PCIe 4.0 x16 on an ASRock Rack ROMED8-2T (EPYC 7313P). The GPUs are on different root ports (2 hops). `amd-smi topology`: link type PCIE, access ENABLED both ways, cache coherency NC. `can_device_access_peer` True both ways; a 64 MiB `cuda:0 -> cuda:1` copy runs at 25.4 GiB/s.
- Host kernel 7.0.0, `iommu=pt`. vLLM v0.32.0rc2 built from source, torch 2.13.0+rocm10.1.0. The build also carries a few unrelated patches plus #57767 (opt-in, off unless `VLLM_ROCM_USE_RDNA_ALL_REDUCE=1`). This PR applied with one hand-merged hunk in `RocmPlatform.use_custom_allreduce()` (a conflict with #57767), so both are selectable in one image.
- Model: Qwen3.8-27B FP8, TP=2, bf16 KV cache, max-model-len 262144, max-num-seqs 2, max-num-batched-tokens 1024, MTP with 3 speculative tokens, `HSA_ENABLE_IPC_MODE_LEGACY=0` (dma-buf IPC).

**Arms** (same image, fresh server start for every block, startup log checked each time)
| arm | how | startup log |
|---|---|---|
| this PR | default | `Custom allreduce on RDNA4 over PCIe peer-to-peer: release start barrier, messages smaller than 8388608 bytes.` and `Using ['CUSTOM', 'PYNCCL']` |
| #57767 | `VLLM_ROCM_USE_RDNA_ALL_REDUCE=1` | `Enabled graph-only RDNA HIP all-reduce: gfx1201 TP2`, `Using ['RDNA_HIP', 'PYNCCL']` |
| off | `--disable-custom-all-reduce` | `Using ['PYNCCL']` |

All 12 server starts showed the expected line for their arm.

**Decode, MTP3** (t/s, mean ± sd over 3 rounds, arm order rotated each round; llama-benchy pp2048 / tg128, single request; SE = difference / standard error)
| depth | this PR | #57767 | off | PR vs off | PR vs #57767 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 73.70 ± 2.88 | 69.67 ± 2.90 | 69.25 ± 2.61 | +6.4% (2.0 SE) | +5.8% (1.7 SE) |
| 32K | 69.31 ± 1.96 | 65.59 ± 1.13 | 65.65 ± 2.46 | +5.6% (2.0 SE) | +5.7% (2.9 SE) |
| 120K | 57.15 ± 3.64 | 51.69 ± 2.42 | 55.32 ± 2.54 | +3.3% (0.7 SE) | +10.6% (2.2 SE) |

MTP acceptance per block: this PR 68.2 / 69.7 / 69.3%, #57767 67.8 / 65.0 / 67.3%, off 68.3 / 66.8 / 65.7%.

Prefill was about the same (pp2048: 2961 / 2892 / 2886 t/s), as expected since 1024-token prefill chunks are 10 MiB and still go to RCCL.

With MTP3, #57767 was no faster than off. Probably because it only handles graph steps with 1 token per request, so the MTP verify steps (2 requests x 4 tokens x 5120 x bf16 = 80 KiB) go to RCCL, while this PR covers them.

**Decode, MTP off** (t/s, 1 run per arm)
| depth | this PR | #57767 | off |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 35.39 | 34.92 | 33.45 |
| 32K | 32.45 | 32.24 | 30.96 |

**Correctness** (temperature 0, thinking off, same prompts on every arm)
- 30 arithmetic and word questions with known answers: 29/30 on all three arms, same miss on each (702 / 39 answered as 17.99).
- Needle recall at ~100K tokens (needle at 40% depth): found on all arms.
- 5 longer generations (200 tokens each): output identical across all three arms.
- llama-benchy coherence check at concurrency 1 and 2: passed on all arms.

**Stability**
- 10-minute soak on this PR's arm: 109 requests, 0 errors.
- KV cache pool: this PR's arm used 0-8K fewer tokens than off (344-352K vs 352K with MTP3, 404.6K vs 411.9K without MTP). About the same as #57767.

**Tests from this PR** (`tests/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py -k 'producer_in_graph or rdna4 or pcie_p2p or dispatch_max_size'`)
- `test_custom_allreduce_dispatch_max_size` (2), `test_rocm_pcie_p2p_detection` (3), `test_rocm_is_fully_connected_over_pcie_only_on_rdna4` (2): passed.
- `test_custom_allreduce_producer_in_graph` TP=2 (platform_default, release_1stage, release_2stage): passed. TP=4/8 skipped (2 GPUs).
  These first failed at init because of a duplicate import in the #57767 patch I also carry (noted on #57767); they pass with that line removed.
